newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power eases in moderate demand.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power eases in moderate demand.

text.p: Spot bulk power prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) eased Thursday in moderate demand and in line with lower natural gas prices, brokers and marketers said.

ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Friday was said to be talked at $21.50-22.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) from $22.50-23.50 on Wednesday for Thursday delivery, the brokers and marketers said.
Non-firm on peak power for Friday delivery was notionally pegged lower at $19.00-21.00 from $20.00-22.00 per MWh.
Firm off-peak Friday ERCOT deliveries were pegged steady at $13.00-14.00, while non firm off peak power was assessed unchanged at $11.00-13.00, the sources said.
March ERCOT peak power was talked lower at $20.30-20.70 from $20.60-20.90 on Wednesday, while July/August peak power was talked lower from $24.75-24.95 from $24.95-25.25 per MWh, the sources said.
Temperatures in Texas were expected to average five to 10 degrees below normal through the weekend, with some areas reachnig as low as 15 degrees below normal by Saturday.
Spot natural gas prices in Texas were said to have eased Thursday, while natural gas futures also declined.
Also, Houston Lighting and Power's 1,250 megawatt South Texas unit 2 was expected to shut down for planned refueling and maintenance on Feb 7 for a scheduled 35 days.
